issue.title: Bug: wait_until does not properly handle exceptions raised by failed pytest_assert

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Low

### Description of the bug

Found while debugging a different issue:

  - pytest_assert (tests/common/helpers/assertions.py) calls pytest.fail() on
    failure.
  - pytest.fail() raises _pytest.outcomes.Failed, which inherits from
    OutcomeException -> BaseException (NOT Exception).
  - wait_until (tests/common/utilities.py:125) catches only `except Exception`,
    so Failed propagates straight through and aborts the test on the first
    attempt.
  - The wait_until window is therefore effectively dead for mismatch cases.
    Only genuine Exception subclasses are handled correctly and get retried.

The fix appears to be to use a more targeted try/except handler here:

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/master/tests/common/utilities.py#L151

### Steps to Reproduce

This was found while debugging generic_config_updater/test_dynamic_acl.py.  In the case I was investigating, the status output of `show acl table DYNAMIC_ACL` was initially reported as "NA".  This was causing the wait_until wrapping the check to be skipped and the test to be failed outright.

Lib in question is here:

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/master/tests/common/gu_utils.py#L531

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Failures due to pytest_assert invoked from within a wait_until should not cause an immediate test failure (as they do today).  The exception should be handled and the retry mechanism continued.

resolution.title: Handle pytest.fail.Exception in wait_until
resolution.description:
Allow pytest_assert to trigger wait_until retries.

### Description of PR

Summary:
Fixes #24726

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
wait_until already handles Exception, and multiple places in the code assume pytest.fail.Exception is handled as well.  pytest.fail.Exception actually derives from BaseException, which means it is currently unhandled by wait_until, and so will not trigger retries (and immediately fail tests).

#### How did you do it?
Added pytest.fail.Exception to the list of handled exception classes in wait_until.

#### How did you verify/test it?
Manual test run.
